reason: The cited evidence shows intermetallic formation in Mg-containing alloys (E1) and spinodal nanostructures in HEAs (E2), but neither supports the specific claims about spinodal decomposition in Mg-containing HEAs, the beneficial effect of precipitates on corrosion/oxidation, or the coarsening-induced degradation.
premises: Mg-containing HEAs can form intermetallic precipitates upon aging
Spinodal decomposition is a viable mechanism for nanoscale precipitate formation in these alloys
Fine nanoscale precipitates can enhance corrosion and oxidation resistance by refining microstructure and pinning interfaces
Coarsening of precipitates with extended aging leads to deterioration of protective surface films and properties
Aging at 300°C is sufficient to induce these microstructural changes
